faqs.q: What are lifting frames and H-frames used for?
faqs.a: A lifting frame holds a load at four or more points with every bottom sling vertical, and an H-frame is a primary beam with cross beams at each end. A fixed frame suits one load, and an adjustable frame moves its lifting points to suit many.

faqs.q: What do I send to quote a lifting frame or H-frame?
faqs.a: Send the load weight and where its centre of gravity sits, the load's length and width, the positions of its lifting points, the crane hook height and any headroom limit, and where it will work. A drawing, a 3D model or a photo is the quickest start; [our guide to lifting bars for air handling units](/blog/lifting-bars-for-air-handling-units) shows a worked case.

faqs.q: What types of Lifting Frames & H-Frames can be built?
faqs.a: Typical builds are fixed spreader frames and H-frames, adjustable H-frames (castellated, slide and pin), adjustable frames on struts, cross frames with sliding clamps, T-piece frames for three-point loads and heavy-duty custom frames.

faqs.q: Fixed or adjustable frame: which should I choose?
faqs.a: Choose fixed for one load lifted repeatedly and adjustable when the lifting points change from load to load. Adjustable H-frames move their cross beams along castellations, slide and pin, or extend on struts.

faqs.q: What working load limit do the Lifting Frames & H-Frames have?
faqs.a: The listing gives the working load limit as to order, because each frame is designed for the load and lifting points you give. State the capacity and geometry on the RFQ and the rating is confirmed on the general arrangement drawing; the standard modular range is on the [Modular Spreader Frames — 10 t to 90 t](/p/modular-spreader-frames) listing.

faqs.q: What are the Lifting Frames & H-Frames made of and how are they finished?
faqs.a: The Lifting Frames & H-Frames are structural steel, grade to the design, with a paint system to your specification; galvanized for outdoor use can be requested.

faqs.q: Which standard and documents come with the Lifting Frames & H-Frames?
faqs.a: Each frame is designed to EN 13155, load tested before dispatch and supplied with a declaration of conformity, a test certificate and user instructions. ASME B30.20 / BTH-1 or DNV offshore design can be requested, and design calculations, material certificates and witnessed testing can be added.

faqs.q: How are the Lifting Frames & H-Frames rigged and what goes with them?
faqs.a: The frame hangs from top slings to the crane hook and the load hangs from vertical bottom slings at its lifting points. Related equipment is on the [spreader beams](/c/spreader-beams), [lifting beams](/c/lifting-beams) and [container lifting frames](/c/container-lifting-frames).

faqs.q: How is a made-to-order frame approved before it is built?
faqs.a: Your enquiry is reviewed by the maker's design engineers, who issue a general arrangement drawing for your approval before anything is made. After delivery it needs a pre-use check before every lift and periodic thorough examination as your site requires.

faqs.q: How do the Lifting Frames & H-Frames compare with a modular spreader frame?
faqs.a: A made-to-order frame is built to one load or a set of lifting points, while the [Modular Spreader Frames — 10 t to 90 t](/p/modular-spreader-frames) bolts together from corner units and struts to square or rectangular layouts. Choose modular for standard sizes and custom for special loads.

faqs.q: What is the Modular Spreader Frames — 10 t to 90 t used for?
faqs.a: The Modular Spreader Frames — 10 t to 90 t is a four-point spreader frame that keeps every bottom sling vertical, built from four corner units joined by struts from the modular spreader beam range of the matching size. It is set square or rectangular to suit the load, and changed for the next one.

faqs.q: How do I read part numbers such as IH-LR-BH-MSF-10 for the Modular Spreader Frames — 10 t to 90 t?
faqs.a: Each part number is one frame size: IH-LR-BH-MSF-10 is the 10 t frame for up to 4.5 × 4.5 m, IH-LR-BH-MSF-40 the 40 t frame for up to 9 × 9 m and IH-LR-BH-MSF-90 the 90 t frame for up to 14 × 14 m. The frame WLL is the most the whole frame may carry.

faqs.q: What frame sizes and capacities does the Modular Spreader Frames — 10 t to 90 t cover?
faqs.a: The frames run from 10 t, up to 4.5 × 4.5 m, to 90 t, up to 14 × 14 m, in six sizes of 10, 17, 30, 40, 70 and 90 t. The rating for each length and width the frame can be set to is in the configuration chart in the user instructions.

faqs.q: Can I use struts I already have with the Modular Spreader Frames — 10 t to 90 t?
faqs.a: Yes, if they are from the modular spreader beam range of the matching size: add the four corner units and the frame is complete. A full set of struts of the matching size must be used with the corner units.

faqs.q: What does each corner of the Modular Spreader Frames — 10 t to 90 t carry?
faqs.a: Each corner is rated a quarter of the frame WLL, so the 10 t frame carries 2.5 t per corner and the 90 t frame 22.5 t. With an off-centre load, check that the heaviest corner stays within its rating; see [our sling angle and compression force guide](/blog/sling-angle-compression-force) for how angles load the frame.

faqs.q: What are the Modular Spreader Frames — 10 t to 90 t made of and bolted with?
faqs.a: The Modular Spreader Frames — 10 t to 90 t has steel corner units with bolt-in modular struts, joined with grade 8.8 bolts, nuts and washers. The fasteners per joint and torque rise with size, from 4 x M10 x 30 at 80 Nm on the 10 t frame to 6 x M20 x 65 at 160 Nm on the 90 t frame.

faqs.q: Which standard and documents come with the Modular Spreader Frames — 10 t to 90 t?
faqs.a: The Modular Spreader Frames — 10 t to 90 t is listed to EN 13155 and ships with a declaration of conformity and user instructions with a configuration chart. Ask for the chart for your frame size before you plan the lift.

faqs.q: What rigging and parts go with the Modular Spreader Frames — 10 t to 90 t?
faqs.a: Struts come from the matching [spreader beams](/c/spreader-beams), and top and bottom rigging, struts and corner units can be quoted together. Hang the frame from top slings within the angle the chart allows; related equipment is on the [lifting beams](/c/lifting-beams) and [lifting attachments and tools](/c/below-the-hook-attachments).

faqs.q: What are the rules for using the Modular Spreader Frames — 10 t to 90 t?
faqs.a: Load the frame only at its four corner points and never hang a load from a strut. Use the fasteners and torque given for the size, a full set of struts of the matching size, and rig the top slings within the angle the chart allows.

faqs.q: Frame or two spreader beams: how does the Modular Spreader Frames — 10 t to 90 t compare?
faqs.a: A frame keeps all four slings vertical in one rigging layer and needs less headroom than two beams hung under a third. The [Lifting Frames & H-Frames](/p/lifting-frames-h-frames) listing covers fixed and adjustable frames built to a drawing.
